pr.title: Run each draft-state and publish command on a line by itself
pr.head: c95184214f3f6842ca0335c12c1ed45a4ddff9e7

summary: Projector's skills tell agents to move a pull request's draft state with project review hold and project review ready, and to post a review with project review publish. project init adds the allow rule Bash(project *) to the user's Claude Code settings, so these commands run without a prompt and without auto mode judging them.

That rule matches only a line where every command matches an allow rule. Claude Code splits a line on ;, &&, ||, and pipes, so a gh pr view joined to project review ready sends the whole line to auto mode. Auto mode refused one such line as undoing a hold, and the skill then told the agent to stop and ask the user, so the pull request stayed a draft.

This change tells the agent to run each of the three commands on a line by itself, explains why, and says to run a refused joined command again alone before asking the user. A new test fails when any skill's shell example joins one of the three commands to another command.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Hold. project review hold converts a signed-off pull request to a draft while its author builds a change on it, so nobody merges it meanwhile.
  • Allow rule. A Claude Code permission rule, such as Bash(project *), that lets a command run without a prompt.
  • Auto mode. Claude Code's automatic approval, which judges commands no rule decides and can refuse them.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: A Projector review of c951842 found nothing blocking and listed three suggestions: align the subagent bullet in review-pr that says to stop on a refused publish, give project summary publish the same rule, and add the rule where work and cleanup mark a pull request ready.

groups.title: Why a joined line loses the allow rule
groups.kicker: The full rule and its reason, in the skill that holds pull requests
intro: fix-pr fixes review findings on a pull request. When a clean pull request needs a change, it holds the pull request as a draft, pushes the change, and marks it ready again. This group rewrites the passage on those two commands.

The passage now says three things: that each command prints the draft state and the head it acted on, so no gh pr view is needed after it; that a line joining a command to others falls to auto mode because every command on it must match an allow rule; and that a refused joined line is run again as the Projector command alone, with the user asked only when the command was refused by itself.

files.note: The passage under "Hold the pull request while changes are built" that says how to run hold and ready, and what to do when the host refuses one.

checks.text: Each command prints the head. set_draft in src/projector/review.py returns the head it read after the change, and draft_lines prints it, as in marked ninjudd/projector#463 ready for review at c951842.
The rule project init adds is Bash(project *), as the text says: ALLOW in src/projector/permissions.py. Its Codex prefix rules include review hold, ready, and publish.
The new retry is the same command run again alone, not another form of it. A command refused while alone still goes to the user, never to gh pr ready.

groups.title: The skills that point at the rule
groups.kicker: Three skills repeat the rule where they mark ready or publish
intro: implement and spec mark a pull request ready at the hand-over, and review-pr publishes a review. Each said to run its command "as a command of its own", and each now says to run it on a line by itself, joined to no other command, pointing at fix-pr for the reason.
review-pr also gains the retry: a publish refused while joined to other commands runs again alone, and a publish refused alone goes to the user as before.

groups.title: Tests that keep the rule in the skills
groups.kicker: Skill text and shell examples checked for joined commands
intro: test_the_skills_move_draft_state_through_the_commands_alone now checks that fix-pr, implement, and spec say "on a line by itself", and that fix-pr carries the retry sentence.

test_no_skill_example_joins_a_review_command_to_another reads every fenced sh or bash block in every skill. It fails on a line that runs project review ready, hold, or publish beside ;, &&, or a pipe. It strips <…> placeholders first, so <clean|changes-requested> is not read as a pipe.

checks.text: The new test catches the bug it names. With && gh pr view <number> appended to the project review ready example in a copy of fix-pr, it fails on &&.
